Happycoding Everyday
Your DeepSeek Harness activity as a GitHub-style contribution graph.
English | 中文

*Display name **Happycoding Everyday**; the package, the repository and the
plugin id stay `dsh-happ

name **Happycoding Everyday**; the package, the repository and the
plugin id stay `dsh-happycode`.*

Happycoding Everyday reads the session logs DeepSeek Harness already writes on
your machine, turns t

hem into one number per day, and draws the year the way
GitHub draws it: weeks across, Monday to Sun

day down, five shades of green, a
tooltip on every cell. It is a plugin, not a service — nothing lea

hades of green, a
tooltip on every cell. It is a plugin, not a service — nothing leaves the machine.
## Install

From the DSH plugin market, search **Happycoding Everyday** and install it in one
click. From a term

the DSH plugin market, search **Happycoding Everyday** and install it in one
click. From a terminal:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

On DSH Desktop, install it from **Settings → Plugins** instead (the app owns that
profile). Restart

DSH once so the server half loads. Afterwards the client half
reloads with the page.

Then open your **avatar menu** at the bottom of the sidebar. `HappyCode` sits
between **Settings** a

nd **Feedback** — the menu keeps the short name, the dialog
carries the full one.
## What you get

- **A row in the account menu** — same typography, spacing and hover state as the
three rows around

it, with a small heat-grid glyph.
- **A profile row** — a 120px avatar, your name at 24px and `Codin

g since Oct 2026`
beside it, read from the account launcher the host already rendered. No picture?
T

he first letter on a brand-coloured tile. No account at all? The row is not
drawn. Never your e-mail

: the host only exposes a masked one, so an `@` means
"no name".
- **A dialog that matches the host'

s own Settings dialog** — the brand centred in a
90px title band, close button in the top-right corn

er, Escape and a click on the
backdrop. Its height follows the content (`min(1500px, 94vw)` wide, ca

pped at
88vh) instead of reserving empty space.
- **One view: a calendar year.** January to December

, Monday-based columns, blank
padding cells at both ends so no neighbouring year leaks in.
- **A gra

ph that fills the dialog.** Cell size is computed from the card's width —
21px at the design width,

14px floor — and recomputed whenever the window
changes, so there is no dead space to the right of t

he grid.
- **Readable axis labels** — `Jan`…`Dec` and `Mon`/`Wed`/`Fri` at 18px.
- **GitHub's legend

, in GitHub's place** — inside the card, under the grid, right
aligned.
- **A year picker** on the r

ight of the card — the current year plus the years
with activity, newest first, capped at three. A n

ew year still gets a button,
even before it has any activity.
- **A tooltip on every cell** — `19 co

ntributions on October 24th.` and
`No contributions on October 23rd.`, GitHub's wording, with ordina

ls.
- **The GitHub palette** in both light and dark, following the host theme.
- **Weights you can c

hange** — three numbers and a **Recalculate** button on the
plugin's page under **Plugins**.
## What counts
One contribution value per day, from three kinds of event in the session log:
| Event | Weight | Default |

| A message you sent (`user/message` with a real user source) | `m` | 1 |
| A tool call (`tool/call`

) | `t` | 1 |
| A tool call that writes a file (`write`, `edit`, `str_replace_editor`, …) | `f` | 3

| `t` | 1 |
| A tool call that writes a file (`write`, `edit`, `str_replace_editor`, …) | `f` | 3 |
`value = 1·m + 1·t + 3·f`

Deliberately **not** counted: injected context (runtime snapshots, skill catalogs,
time context), as

sistant messages, tool results, sub-agent sessions, and empty
sessions. The rules and the evidence b

ehind them live in
docs/data-schema.md.

Colours are bucketed from your own data: the 25th/50th/75th percentile of the
non-zero days **inside

the current window** become the three thresholds. Fewer
than eight active days, or quartiles that c

ollapse onto each other, fall back to
GitHub's fixed `1–9 / 10–19 / 20–39 / 40+`.
## Privacy

- **No network requests.** The plugin talks to the host over its own loopback
HTTP routes and nothin

g else. No telemetry, no fonts, no avatars fetched.
- **Read-only on your logs.** `~/.dsh/sessions/`

and the session projection cache
are only ever read.
- **One writable directory**: `~/.dsh/profiles

/<profile>/.dsh-happycode/`, holding
`daily.json`, `sessions.json` and `settings.json`.
- **No log c

ontent is written anywhere.** Diagnostics carry file names, counts and
error messages only.
## Compatibility

- DSH `0.2.1` or newer, prereleases included (`engines.dsh: ">=0.2.1-0"` — the
account menu and the

plugin configuration page are what it targets).
- Node `22.15` or newer, for the built-in Zstandard

decoder. On an older Node the
compressed logs are skipped and logged rather than crashing.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The first index runs in the background; afterwards only sessions whose size or
mtime changed are dec

oded again. A session that fails to decode is skipped and
counted in the status, never retried and n

A session that fails to decode is skipped and
counted in the status, never retried and never fatal.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The client bundle is hand-written CommonJS in `client/client.js` — no build step.
It registers itsel

f with the host's `window.__ModuleLoader__` and requires only
`react` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-u
i-primitives` from the host's module table.

See docs/host-ui-notes.md for how the account-menu row is
injected and why.
